meta.title: hexa-lang — Architecture (SSOT)
meta.role: Single source of truth for the final architecture
meta.retired_md: ARCHITECTURE.md is retired to a 1-line SSOT pointer stub (2026-06-16); this JSON is the SSOT, humans read architecture.html

blocks.text: `hexa-lang` is a self-hosted native compiler for the `.hexa` language, shipped with the `hx` package manager. There is **no LLVM anywhere in the toolchain**. The self-host backend lowers source directly through its own IR to native objects (ELF64 / Mach-O arm64) and links them with its own linker (`hexa_ld`); this native-emit path is a proven byte-identical fixpoint (`gen3 ≡ gen4`) and is the default for `--emit`. Two pieces of C still remain — see Self-host status for the honest accounting: a C-transpile **fallback delegate** still serves some full `hexa build`/`run` flows until the native end-to-end path lands, and a ~5.5k-LOC **C runtime substrate** (the libc/syscall bootstrap floor, generated from `.hexa` emitter SSOTs) is compiled and linked into every binary. This substrate is **reducible**: a 2026-06-16 falsification (`.verdicts/zeroc-breakthrough/`) showed ~50% of `runtime_core.c` is pure-algorithm code portable to `.hexa` today (a `.hexa` `hexa_fnv1a` is byte-identical to the C one), the syscall layer is `@asm`-svc eliminable, and the genuine residual is only libm transcendentals + GPU FFI — so zero-`.c` is an **open, attackable campaign**, not a policy that accepts C permanently.

Its defining feature is an embedded **atlas** — a ~4.2 MB theorem dictionary (P primitives / C constants / L laws / E errors) baked statically into the binary. Every formula-bearing function must either cite an atlas law (`@cite(L[id])`), carry an active `@verify`, or declare an explicit `@grace`; otherwise the build refuses to produce a binary (stage S8, fatal `HX8004`). Enforcement happens at the **build gate**, not at runtime — the atlas adds 0 ms of runtime cost.

The compiler runs eight ordered strict-lint stages (S0 parse → S1 resolve → S2 bind → S3 type → S4 domain → S5 units → S6 equational `@verify` → S7 proof `@prove` → S8 citation). A binary appears only when every fatal stage passes. After the gate, source is lowered HIR → MIR (SSA) → LIR and emitted per target. The compiler is self-hosting: the compiler that builds `.hexa` is itself written in `.hexa` (`self/`).
Honest accounting of where self-hosting actually stands (no overclaim — `git log` + the `.verdicts/` tree are the evidence):

rows: Native-emit backend (own IR → Mach-O / ELF, no LLVM)

items: ✅ **x86_64 RUNG 2** (done 2026-06-15) — `print("hi")` now prints `hi` via the native x86_64 emitter. The HexaVal 16-byte SysV reg-pair ABI landed in #3340; the string-payload `lea` was then dropped in the native-emit data-address matcher (it only saw bare `.LCstrN` labels, not the `[rip+<label>]`-wrapped payload) — fixed by `_ex86_data_label_of` (`compiler/emit/elf_x86_64.hexa`). verdict `F-X86-RUNG2-STRING-PRINT-PASS`.

✅ **Full native `hexa build` end-to-end** (done 2026-06-15) — `hexa build <src> -o OUT` now produces a native executable with **zero clang / zero system ld**: the `hx-selfhost-cli` launcher's new `build` route (native-first + delegate-fallback, mirroring the `run` route #3325) runs `gen3 --emit=obj` → `hexa_ld <obj> rt.o -o OUT`. Corpus-verified (arith/string/loop/fn/cond/array 6/6) + standing gate `tool/selfhost_native_build_gate` (`.github/workflows/selfhost-native-build-gate.yml`). Safety: any program gen3/hexa_ld can't build, `HEXA_NATIVE_BUILD=0`, or an unknown flag → falls through to the shipped build (builds never break); reversible via `promote_selfhost.sh --revert`. verdict `F-SELFHOST-NATIVE-BUILD-FLIP`. (The deeper `self/main.hexa cmd_build` `--emit=asm`→clang block is left intact as the fallback — the launcher route already delivers clang-free builds without a gen3 rebuild / shipped-toolchain blast risk.)

blocks.title: Runtime C floor (reducible — zero-C campaign OPEN, not "irreducible")

blocks.text: `self/runtime*.c` (~23.6k LOC across `runtime.c` + `runtime_core.c` + `runtime_hi_gen.c`; the doc's older "~5.5k tier-A" figure undercounted) is generated from `*_emit.hexa` SSOTs, not authored by hand. **CORRECTION (2026-06-16):** the prior M3 verdict's claim that this floor is *irreducible* with *zero portable surface* was **FALSIFIED**. M3 reached "irreducible" by tallying M1 reason-columns on paper — it never tested whether a pure leaf actually ports, nor the `@asm`-svc syscall path the compiler's own `PLAN.md` flags as eliminable. Falsification (verdict `.verdicts/zeroc-breakthrough/F-ZEROC-M3-OVERCLAIM-FALSIFIED.txt`):

items: **Proven port** — `hexa_fnv1a` (pure uint32 XOR/mul loop) reimplemented in pure `.hexa` is **byte-identical** to the C function over 6 cases (incl. the string "no .c 완전돌파"). So "zero portable hexa leaves" is false.

**Portable surface is large** — a per-function body audit of `runtime_core.c` finds **155 of 308 top-level fns (50%) call no libc/libm/syscall** → portable to `.hexa` today, zero toolchain change. (`libc-dep:140` is mostly `malloc`/`memcpy` convenience that itself ports once a `.hexa` arena + `memcpy`-loop exist; `syscall-dep:3`; `libm/FFI-dep:10`.)

**Roadmap agrees** — `PLAN.md` L7589/L8183/L8341 mark kernel syscalls as eliminable; the compiler already emits byte-correct `svc #0x80` / x86 `syscall` (as the program's exit), and a `__fd_write_bytes` builtin exists. ⚠️ *Honest caveat:* the existing `@asm` block (`stdlib/firmware/asm.hexa`) emits a GCC `__asm__` **C** fragment for **cortex-M only** — it is a C-transpile firmware feature, NOT a native-emit syscall surface. Native zero-C therefore needs a **new** general syscall intrinsic (`@syscall(num, args…)` → `svc`/`syscall` with register marshalling); that's buildable codegen work, not a wall (Z2 in the campaign).

blocks.text: The **honest** floor is therefore NOT "all ~5.5k LOC". It reduces to (a) **libm transcendentals** (~10 fns — a policy choice for FP-codegen fragility, not a hard wall), (b) **raw syscall instruction emission** (proven; needs the `@asm`-svc general lowering wired for the runtime — designed, partial), and (c) **GPU/device FFI** (tier-C, outside the compiler's self-host scope). `ls self/*.c` empty is thus an **attackable codegen campaign**, not "unreachable by porting".

**RT-NATIVE Z2a DONE (2026-06-16):** `runtime_hi_gen.c` is eliminated on the default arm64-darwin build (`ls self/*.c` 3→2) — `rt_str_*` come from a native-compiled object (the frozen `self/native/runtime_hi_native.s` seed), byte-identical + runtime-verified, self-host fixpoint preserved. x86_64-linux keeps the C path pending its codegen value-model rework. Full zero-`.c` remains multi-step (port batches + `@asm`-syscall wiring + a libm decision), much of it pod-gated — but the wall ("can't be done") is broken. Tracked: **RT-NATIVE domain** (`RT-NATIVE.md`, 8 milestones Z0–Z5; supersedes the HEXA-BUILDFLOOR zero-C tracking). **awk-synth regen (2026-06-17, #3455/#3457):** the linux gen.c path's flaky hexat-regen is replaced by a deterministic awk un-escape of the `*_emit.hexa` SSOT (casefold/trim + trim-ends groups, CI faithful 3-job green) — a BUILD-STABILITY fix, not an `ls` reduction (gen.c stays a C build-artifact on linux). **Honest leg-B accounting:** `self/*.c` are all gitignored build artifacts (clean checkout = `ls self/*.c == ∅`); the real ls-reduction lever for linux is a **native `.s` seed** (Darwin already has `runtime_hi_native.s`; x86_64/linux lacks one). With x86_64 codegen graduated (#3431/#3432), `aprime --emit=asm --target=x86_64-linux` can bake `self/runtime_hi.hexa` into an x86_64 `.s` seed, letting `stage_resolve_runtime_a`'s `HEXA_ZEROC_RT_HI` path drop the linux gen.c too — the next leg-B unit. **x86_64 native seed BLOCKED (2026-06-17, root cause confirmed on aiden):** the linux x86_64 `runtime_hi` native seed (PR #3460) fails at runtime — the x86_64 codegen's documented "raw-int model" (x86_64_linux.hexa:636-640) carries only the payload register and derives the HexaVal tag from the operand kind, so a string stored in a local is tagged TAG_INT(0); a tag-dispatching helper (hexa_len `if HX_IS_STR`) then sees tag=0 and returns 0, and every native function taking a HexaVal string argument returns empty/null (C-harness: 9/9). arm64 carries the full {tag,payload} 16-byte pair via stp/ldp, preserving the tag — which is why the arm64 darwin seed works and x86_64 does not. self-emit byte-eq (#3432) and int-only RUNG tests pass because they are tag-independent, so they never caught the runtime-ABI defect. The x86_64 native seed is therefore blocked until the x86_64 backend value-model is reworked to carry full HexaVal pairs (verdict F-LEGB-X86-SEED-TAGLOSS-ROOTCAUSE). **FIXED + LANDED (2026-06-17, #3462):** the x86_64 backend value-model was reworked to carry the full HexaVal {tag,payload} pair like arm64 (x86_64_linux.hexa +499L: pair ingress, per-value tag-slot, call box/unbox, rax:rdx pair return; plus two regalloc bugs the pair model exposed — rax removed from the caller-saved alloc pool, and loop-back-edge liveness extended to [0,pos]). Verified by full CI (12/12 green, not self-report): C-differential harness 9/9 (was 9/9 null), faithful-nobaseline linux-x86_64 (the previously-RED job) PASS, linux-arm64 + darwin-arm64 PASS (untouched), and selfhost-byteeq-real (whole-compiler gen3≡gen4) PASS at a new SHA. The new x86_64 ELF seed self/native/runtime_hi_x86_64.s ships with HEXA_ZEROC_RT_HI=1 default, so runtime_hi_gen.c is now eliminated on x86_64-linux too (parity with darwin). **rt_str hexa-source-complete (2026-06-17, F-LEGB-RTSTR-HEXASOURCE-COMPLETE):** a grep audit falsified the "next rt_str group" premise — every rt_str function (index_of/substr/slice/parse_int/parse_float/…) already has a hexa-source definition in self/rt/string.hexa · stdlib/runtime/ctype.hexa · self/runtime_pure.hexa (the runtime_core.c `extern`s just reference them), so genuine C-only rt_str = 0. The real remaining ls-reduction is NOT porting more rt_str groups but **standalone #else removal**: the runtime.c/runtime_core.c `#else` (standalone) C-body fallbacks duplicate the now-native hexa-source and hold the file; making the standalone build always link the hexa-source rt_*.o lets those #else blocks be deleted (a build redesign, not a research wall). **Standalone-#else liveness — LIVE, honest NO-GO (2026-06-17, verdict `F-LEGB-STANDALONE-ELSE-NOGO`):** a captured-output liveness probe (c2) settled whether the standalone (non-`HEXA_HAS_HEXA_RT_STDLIB`) `#else` C-bodies are dead code. **They are LIVE and PRIMARY** — `tool/release_build` → `tool/stage_resolve_runtime_a:271` compiles `self/runtime.c` with `CFLAGS=-O2 -std=gnu11 -D_GNU_SOURCE -Wno-trigraphs` (NO `-DHEXA_HAS_HEXA_RT_STDLIB`) into `build/runtime.a`, which every CI gate funneling through `release_build` consumes (selfhost-byteeq-gate, release.yml, miscompile-zero-gate, determinism-gate). aiden measurement: the actual CI builder `CC=gcc bash tool/stage_resolve_runtime_a` produces a 551566B `runtime.a` with **33 `rt_*` DEFINED (T)** = the `#else` C-bodies (vs gate-ON: 21 DEFINED, 155 UNDEFINED/delegated). So the `#else` bodies are NOT removable dead code — deleting them would leave `build/runtime.a` with undefined `rt_*` and break the live `./hexa` link. This **corrects the earlier `F-LEG-B-DEADCODE-PATH` claim** ("standalone = dead code, 0 real builds use it"), which surveyed only the `build_aprime`/`build_native_*` (HEXA_HAS=1) family and missed `stage_resolve_runtime_a`. Two build families coexist: aprime (HEXA_HAS=1, hexa-source delegation) and release/standalone (#else C-body, PRIMARY shipping). The `#else` is a Go/Rust-equivalent freestanding substrate (honest-keep, c9). leg-B `ls self/*.c == ∅` therefore needs ①porting the ~1190 common core fns to hexa-native (multi-session) + ②a standalone-build ABI redesign so it links hexa-source rt_*.o (HexaVal↔float wrappers per `F-LEG-B-STANDALONE-SCOPE`) — NOT a simple `#else` deletion. **x86_64 generic index + arithmetic-binop tag-dispatch FIXED (2026-06-17, fn-param numeric-array indexing tag-corruption, c1):** the #3462 pair-model reworked the runtime-SEED value model, but the x86_64 backend (`compiler/codegen/x86_64_linux.hexa`) was still missing two GENERIC source-level lowerings that arm64_darwin.hexa already had. (1) The `_STMT_ASSIGN` dispatch had NO `op="index"`/`op="index_set"` branch, so `a[i]` fell through to the default-assign that copies the BASE container payload (carrying TAG_ARRAY) — the index was silently dropped, so a numeric fn-param array element came back as the array pointer tagged 24/garbage (`tag 24` corruption, segfault on int-add of two pointers); added handlers routing through `hexa_index_get`/`hexa_index_set` (landed #3481 f25be1e0a). (2) The `_STMT_BINOP` arithmetic path emitted a raw integer `add`/`sub`/`imul` and hardcoded the result tag to TAG_INT, so float arithmetic returned IEEE-754 BITS tagged INT (`1.0-0.0` printed as `4607182418800017408`); fixed by `_x86_hv_arith_sym` routing `+ - * / %` through the tag-dispatching runtime helpers (`hexa_add_slow`/`hexa_sub`/`hexa_mul`/`hexa_div`/`hexa_mod`, arm64 `_hv_binop_sym` parity; bitwise/comparison/concat keep their fast paths). Verified on real x86_64 (aiden, emit→as→link→RUN): the 3 captured repros pass (l2 param-float-array=1.0, f param-int-array=7, let-float-array=5.0) + int/float arithmetic + param-array distance + loop array-index regression corpus all correct + M1 x86 leaf gate PASS. x86_64-ONLY change → the arm64 byte-eq fixpoint (all CI gates run on arm64-apple-darwin) is structurally unaffected.

**leg A byte-eq fixpoint re-established BOTH targets (2026-06-16):** arm64 native obj `gen3 ≡ gen4` (#3412) + x86_64-linux `gen3 ≡ gen4` asm byte-identical (261,888L sha 94df25cb) + as-clean (#3431/#3432). The memory's "x86_64 RUNG2/codegen immature" claim was FALSIFIED and 7 codegen bugs were fixed (global operand · idiv · wide-imm · test · push · negative-const). verdict `F-X86-GEN3-GEN4-BYTEEQ`.

**leg B boundary-sized + mechanism PROVEN (2026-06-16, verdict `F-LEGB-FLOOR-SIZED-MECHANISM-CONFIRMED`):** `ls self/*.c == ∅` is not a research wall but the VOLUME of a verified mechanism. (a) irreducible floor is **small** — syscall/asm 8 (→ `__hx_syscall0/6` intrinsic built) · libm extern 10 (CLAUDE.md "trig=libm" FFI allowed) · HexaVal struct def 15 (`self/runtime.h` git-tracked, expressible). (b) remaining ~580 fns = dispatch/value-op volume. (c) the C→native-obj swap mechanism is PROVEN — `stage_resolve_runtime_a`'s `HEXA_ZEROC_RT_HI=1` path already `ar`s `build/rt_hi_native.o` into runtime.a and removes the C `#include` (Z2a-done). Core native accumulation 18/591 via leaf intrinsics this session.

**UNLOCK-2 nanbox-constructor intrinsic — GO, already executed; no circularity (2026-06-17, verdict `F-LEGB-UNLOCK2-NANBOX-FEASIBILITY`):** the census category-(1) functions (`hexa_int/float/bool/void`, `hexa_bits_to_float`) are 16-byte tagged-union constructors (`{.tag=TAG_*, .payload}`). A bounded feasibility probe asked whether expressing them in `.hexa` via an `@tag`-style intrinsic creates a bootstrap circularity (the intrinsic needing the constructor it defines). **Answer: NO** — the landed `__hx_tag`/`__hx_payload_*` intrinsics (CHANGELOG "UNLOCK-2 DONE") lower **directly to register `movz`/`mov`/`ldp` writes with zero `bl` (no runtime call)**; `arm64_darwin.hexa::_hv_load` (1090) already inlines every constructor (`const_int → movz lo,#0(TAG_INT)+hi`, `const_bool → movz #2`, `const_void → #4`, `const_float → #1`). The intrinsic IS the constructor body inlined; it bottoms out in the register file + immediate-move opcode, not a HexaVal call — so the recursion never closes. Verified by 3/3 aprime byte-identical fixpoint preservation. This is GO-class (the nanbox constructor is NOT part of the irreducible floor), and unblocks the Z2c dispatch core (`hexa_type_of` = `switch on __hx_tag`). Scope: 6 runtime_core.c fns + ~6 STMT_CALL codegen cases, all arm64-DONE; the only parity gap is the x86_64 backend, which carries the full {tag,payload} pair model (#3462) but has **zero `__hx_*` leaf intrinsics** (measured `grep -c __hx_ x86_64_linux.hexa` = 0) — a bounded single-file mirror. Honest caveat (c9): porting these constructors does NOT reduce `ls self/*.c`; the file count is held by the standalone `#else` blocks (a build redesign, ING #14–16), orthogonal to this intrinsic.

**RT-NATIVE-ZEROC M1 — x86_64 `__hx_*` leaf-intrinsic parity DONE (2026-06-17, verdict `F-M1-X86-LEAF-PARITY`):** the x86_64-linux backend was brought to leaf-intrinsic parity with arm64_darwin.hexa. Gap inventory (c2): `grep __hx_ x86_64_linux.hexa` returned ZERO — all 25 whitelisted `__hx_*` leaves (the arm64 UNLOCK-2..11 STMT_CALL special-cases) were missing. All 25 ported ADD-ONLY (+~330 lines; runtime.c/#else untouched, zero bootstrap risk): tag-read, int compares (cmp+setcc+movzx), int arith (add/sub/imul), FP arith (movq GPR↔xmm + addsd/subsd/mulsd/divsd), FP compares (comisd + seta/setae, **NaN-correct** per the GCC -O1 ordered idiom — `<`→comisd b,a;seta, `<=`→comisd b,a;setae, false-on-unordered, mirroring arm64 MI/LS), to_double (cvtsi2sd + cmove branchless tag-select), str_byte (movzx byte ptr), arr_len (mov r10d, dword ptr [r10+8]), syscall0/6 (Linux ABI rdi/rsi/rdx/r10/r8/r9, num→rax), and ptr_store/load 64/32. **Enabling root-fix (c1, not a shim):** the x86_64 backend had NO const_float payload path at all (the #3462 pair model carried int/str/bool only), so a float literal resolved to the `imm 0` fallback and every float leaf computed against 0.0; `_x86_op_resolve` + `_x86_64_op_for_operand_st` now materialize a const_float payload as `mov reg, float_to_bits(v)` (the compile-time runtime builtin, GNU as encodes the imm64 mov as `movabs`), matching arm64's `.LCfltN: .double` pool value without a float-pool subsystem. Two scratch-discipline bugs were caught by RUNNING (not self-judged) and fixed: `__hx_to_double` used a hardcoded `r12` tag-scratch (an allocatable-pool reg → clobbered a live value, corrupting chained float compares) → moved to `rax`; `__hx_syscall6` staged args into pool regs r12-r15/rbx → loads directly into the caller-saved syscall ABI regs. Verified two ways: encoding ground-truth (GNU `as` ↔ objdump byte-match, `scripts/scratch/rt_native/x86_leaf_gate.sh §A`, 31/31) and semantic ground-truth (emit→as→link-C-runtime→RUN on real x86_64: core=16, str=3, arena=5 — mmap(9)/munmap(11) + ptr round-trip). Self-host fixpoint (x86_64 gen3≡gen4) preserved by construction (ADD-ONLY cases). Honest residuals (c9, PRE-EXISTING x86 gaps orthogonal to the leaves, out of M1 scope): const_str→local-assign still materializes a bare-label absolute address (the leaf itself is correct on a direct literal via lea[rip]), and the x86_64 backend has no `unop`/`!` (logical-not) lowering (emits `nop`) — both are M2 follow-ups. This is the M4 (native runtime-core port) foundation on x86_64.

**RT-NATIVE-ZEROC M4 B1 (nanbox-ctor) — mechanism DONE, file-drop BLOCKED-on-M5, `stdlib/runtime/nanbox.hexa` NOT viable (2026-06-17, verdict `F-M4-B1-NANBOX`):** M4 batch B1 set out to port the census category-(1) constructors (`hexa_int/float/bool/void/bits_to_float/enum_str/enum_str_v`) to a new aprime-compiled `stdlib/runtime/nanbox.hexa`; the premise was corrected by verification. The constructors are already native **three ways**: (a) codegen `_hv_load` (arm64_darwin.hexa:1090) inlines every int/float/bool/void literal to `movz tag` + payload register writes with zero runtime call; (b) a `HEXA_RT_SELFEMIT` byte-emitter (`self/codegen/runtime_arm64.hexa` `rt_hexa_*`, six 12-byte = 3-aarch64-instruction sequences bundled by `test/native_build/emit_hexa_val_ctors_o.hexa`, byte-confirmed vs `as -arch arm64` + JIT-exec-correct); (c) the `__hx_*` read-side intrinsics. A fresh C-differential gate (`scripts/scratch/rt_native/b1_nanbox_gate.c`) links the STANDALONE `runtime.c` (the PRIMARY CI config) and asserts the 16-byte {tag,payload} image of every constructor over negatives, INT64_MIN/MAX, NaN/±inf/±0/DBL_MAX/MIN, true/false, void, and enum pointers, plus decodes the arm64 `rt_hexa_*` byte sequences to their exact encodings + TAG_* immediates — **GATE PASS 35/35, 0 fails on real x86_64 (aiden)**, not self-judged. **`stdlib/runtime/nanbox.hexa` is NOT viable (c9, empirical):** transpiling `fn f(n:int)->HexaVal { HexaVal{tag:0,payload:n} }` via `./build/hexat` emits `HexaVal(hexa_int(0), n)` — a HexaVal struct-literal in hexa source CALLS `hexa_int`, the very constructor (self-recursive). As `numeric.hexa` notes, "hexa typing doesn't model the HexaVal union directly"; the constructors live below the type system (raw register pair), so only a byte-emitter or codegen intrinsic can express them (the twin of the `F-LEGB-RTSTR` already-native finding). No redundant/circular file was authored (c10). **`#else` drop-verdict = NO, keep until M5 (c9):** the authoritative byteeq/release path (`release_build` → `stage_resolve_runtime_a:271`) links the standalone `runtime.c`, whose `nm` shows `hexa_int/float/bool/void/bits_to_float/enum_str` all DEFINED (strong T); deleting the `#else` bodies leaves them undefined and breaks the live `./hexa` link. They stay until M5 (`build_runtime_a_from_source` links native `rt_*.o` into the standalone `runtime.a` + excises the `#else` + a frozen-seed bump). Runtime/emitter unchanged (ADD-only gate + verdict), so the self-host fixpoint is structurally preserved on both targets.

**RT-NATIVE-ZEROC M4 B4 (array-core) — mechanism-BLOCKED (construct WALL-1 + alloc WALL-2), file-drop BLOCKED-on-M5, `stdlib/runtime/array_core.hexa` NOT viable; unblocking lever NAMED = `__hx_make_val` (2026-06-17, verdict `F-M4-B4-ARRAY`):** M4 batch B4 set out to port the array-core family (`hexa_array_new/get/set/push/pop/reserve/snapshot_array`) to a new aprime-compiled `stdlib/runtime/array_core.hexa` using the M1 raw-mem intrinsics; the premise was corrected by verification — B4 is the twin of B1 plus an additional allocation wall. The exact layout was measured (c2): `HexaArr{items@0, len@8, cap@16}` sizeof 24, `HexaVal{tag@0, payload@8}` sizeof 16, element stride 16, negative `cap` = arena sentinel, capacity-doubling ladder 8/16/32/64. **WALL-1 (CONSTRUCT, the B1 twin):** `hexa_array_get/pop/new` return a 16-byte HexaVal ELEMENT, but there is no `(tag,payload)→HexaVal` constructor intrinsic — every `__hx_*` leaf BOXES its result as TAG_INT/BOOL/FLOAT (grep-confirmed in both backends + `self/codegen.hexa`), so a raw payload-word load returns `hexa_int(word)` and the element's real tag is lost and cannot be re-stamped; and `arr[idx]` in hexa source lowers to `hexa_index_get(arr,idx)` (RAN `build/hexat` probe) — a call back into the C runtime = self-recursive/circular. **WALL-2 (ALLOC):** `hexa_array_new` = `calloc`, `push`/`reserve` = `realloc` + the arena subsystem (`__hexa_val_mark_top`, `hexa_array_arena_alloc_items`, negative-cap sentinel) + `hexa_val_heapify` (push-escape analysis) + `_hx_stats_*`, `snapshot_array` = arena→heap promote — none of malloc/calloc/realloc/arena/heapify is intrinsic-expressible (genuine substrate). A fresh C-differential gate (`scripts/scratch/rt_native/b4_array_gate.c`) links the STANDALONE `runtime.c` (the PRIMARY CI config) and drives the live array fns through empty/single/capacity-doubling (40 pushes → cap 64)/set+get/mixed-tag (str+float)/pop/reserve(128)/heap-backed snapshot-identity, asserting the struct layout and the raw 16-byte {tag,payload} image of every stored element — **GATE PASS 32/32, 0 fails on real x86_64 (summer)**, not self-judged; this locks the byte-eq + layout oracle a native object must reproduce. **`stdlib/runtime/array_core.hexa` is NOT viable (c9):** authoring it would be circular/redundant, so none was written (c10). **`#else` drop-verdict = NO, keep until M5 (c9):** the gate LINKED that standalone `runtime.c` successfully, proving the C array bodies are LIVE — deleting them breaks the `release_build` `./hexa` link. **Unblocking lever (NAMED):** `__hx_make_val(tag,payload)→HexaVal` — the symmetric write-half of `__hx_tag`; ADD-only on both backends + C-mirror + bind whitelist, fixpoint structurally preserved, and the single lever that turns the B4/B5 element returns AND the B1 `nanbox.hexa` file-reduction (`hexa_int = __hx_make_val(0,n)`) from blocked to viable (WALL-2 alloc remains separate — needs B2 arena + a malloc-floor decision). Runtime/emitter unchanged (ADD: gate.c + verdict), self-host fixpoint structurally preserved on both targets. **NEXT (array lane r2)** = the `__hx_make_val` constructor-intrinsic micro-PR.

**RT-NATIVE-ZEROC M4 PTR8 — `__hx_ptr_store8`/`__hx_ptr_load8` byte raw-mem leaves DONE (2026-06-17, verdict `F-M4-PTR8`):** M1 landed ptr_load/store 64/32 (#3478); the 8-bit byte pair was the one gap in M2's raw-mem set, needed for `hexa_strbuf_dup_n`'s byte-write (batch B3). `__hx_ptr_store8(addr,off,val)` writes the LOW BYTE of val to [addr+off] (returns addr, chainable); `__hx_ptr_load8(addr,off)` reads the byte ZERO-EXTENDED. Surgical (c10): bind whitelist +2; arm64 codegen `strb w5,[x1]`/`ldrb w1,[x1]` (ldrb = the byte-load encoding proven by `__hx_str_byte`, W-write zero-extends); x86 codegen `mov byte ptr [r10], sil`/`movzx r10, byte ptr [r10]` (movzx byte = proven by str_byte); a new **STRB native object encoder in macho_arm64.hexa** (base `0x39000000 | imm<<10 | rn<<5 | rt`, mirroring the pre-existing LDRB `0x39400000`); self/codegen.hexa C-mirror (`*(uint8_t*)` store / `(int64_t)*(uint8_t*)` load — uint8 cast = no sign-ext). Verified two ways (c2): encoding ground-truth GNU `as`↔objdump — x86 store `41 88 32`, x86 load `4d 0f b6 12`, arm64 `strb=39000025`/`ldrb=39400021`, 4/4 byte-match; semantic ground-truth emit→as→link→RUN on real x86_64 (summer) exit=7 — stores 0x00/0x7F/0xFF/0x80, reads back **0xFF→255 (NOT -1), 0x80→128 (NOT -128) = ZERO-EXTEND confirmed**, + low-byte-only write (511→255) + adjacent-byte isolation + chainable return. Self-host fixpoint (gen3≡gen4) preserved by construction (ADD-ONLY; the compiler never calls `__hx_ptr_*`); CI selfhost-byteeq-real authoritative. Honest residual (c9, PRE-EXISTING M1-wide, not introduced by ptr8): the native x86_64 ELF object emitter does NOT parse the `byte`/`dword`/`qword ptr` size-prefix mem-operand, so `--emit=obj` of any raw-mem leaf (str_byte/ptr32/ptr64/ptr8) ENCODE-MISSes — M1 validated only via `--emit=asm`→GNU as; the asm-text codegen, C-transpile, and fixpoint are unaffected, and arm64 (bracket-only operands) emits to native object fine. Extending the ELF size-prefix parser is a separate M1-wide unit. M2 raw-mem set now complete (64/32/8 store+load).

**RT-NATIVE-ZEROC M5 PILOT (rt_str) — drop-mechanism ALREADY PROVEN+SHIPPED, honest ALREADY-DONE (2026-06-17, verdict `F-M5-PILOT-RTSTR`):** the M5 pilot set out to prove the `.c`-content-drop end-to-end on one already-native family (`rt_str`): make the STANDALONE build link the native `rt_str_*.o` + excise the matching `#else` C bodies + keep byteeq-real green. **Measurement on aiden (real x86_64, the EXACT CI/release builder `CC=gcc bash tool/stage_resolve_runtime_a`) falsifies the task premise that the rt_str `#else` bodies are still LIVE.** The cumulative Z2a campaign (#3455 casefold/trim · #3457 trim-ends · #3465 search-predicates `_b`) ALREADY did exactly this: (1) `resolve_native_rt_hi_seed` runs UNCONDITIONALLY and auto-enables `HEXA_ZEROC_RT_HI=1` whenever a target native `.s` seed exists (it does for darwin-arm64 + linux-x86_64), so the native path is the live default in the STANDALONE config (not an opt-in); (2) the emitter (`self/runtime_core_emit.hexa`) has the rt_str casefold/trim/contains/search-predicate `#else` C bodies RETIRED — the body count for the 8 named fns is **0** on main vs **3** at `d99ecc321^` (pre-#3455); (3) `build_runtime_a_from_source` sed-removes the `runtime_hi_gen.c` `#include` and `ar`s the native `build/rt_hi_native.o` (14 `rt_str_*` syms) into `runtime.a`. Captured (c2): `nm build/runtime.o` shows only the 2 int-return BRIDGE wrappers (`rt_str_starts_with`/`rt_str_ends_with`) as `T`; the 8 task-named fns (to_upper/to_lower/trim/trim_start/trim_end/starts_with_b/ends_with_b/contains_b + casefold) are EXTERN-only (bodies in the `.o`); `runtime_core.c`=411120B; the standalone link resolves all `rt_str_*` with NO undefined symbol; **byteeq-real CI is GREEN on current main** (selfhost-byteeq-gate.yml = the STANDALONE config). So M5-for-rt_str is DONE and the drop-mechanism the pilot was meant to demonstrate is the live default — it is NOT a fake or blocked milestone for this family. **Lone residual (c16, deferred not faked):** the 2 int-return bridges' standalone `#ifndef` branch is genuine self-contained C (`hxlcl_strncmp`/`strcmp`) that the codegen emits (`self/codegen.hexa:442/445`, `arm64_darwin.hexa:1456/1457` "→ int (box bool)"); the native seed exports only the HexaVal-return `_b` form, so the bridge has NO native body to migrate — it is an ABI adapter below the type system (twin of the F-M4-B1 nanbox-ctor finding). Dropping it needs either 2 new hand-assembled int-return seed functions across BOTH ABIs (ELF `runtime_hi_x86_64.s` + Mach-O `runtime_hi_native.s`) OR a codegen call-site change to emit `rt_str_*_b` + inline bool-box — both leave the proven "excise `#else` + `ar` native `.o`" template and risk byteeq divergence, so per c10/c9 they are a separate codegen/seed micro-unit, not this pilot (no fake drop authored). This RE-CONFIRMS `F-LEGB-RTSTR-HEXASOURCE-COMPLETE` + `F-LEGB-RTCORE-PURE-CANDIDATES-ZERO` (#3468, "Z2a 누적 EXHAUSTED"). No emitter/build-script/seed change → the self-host fixpoint is structurally untouched. The genuine `ls self/*.c == ∅` lever stays M4 (the ~1190 common-core port, on families that HAVE a migratable native body) + a `runtime.c`/`runtime_core.c` substrate redesign — not a per-family pilot; rt_str's drop reduced those two amalgam files' rt_str CONTENT (8 bodies → 0) without removing the container files.

**RT-NATIVE-ZEROC m5 r2 — runtime_core.c standalone-`#else` census 🧱 TERMINAL (per-family-drop lane EXHAUSTED, 2026-06-17, verdict `F-M5-R2-RTCORE-CENSUS`):** the m5 lane asked whether any `runtime_core.c` family still carries a LIVE standalone `#else` C body that is PURE-PORTABLE (migratable native body, no `{tag,payload}` construct wall, no malloc/arena wall) — the would-be first non-string `ls`-reduction via the proven Z2a native-seed drop template. A full static census (c2, RAN parser over the freshly-built generated `self/runtime_core.c`, 8734 L) re-ran r1's marker-filter census (`F-LEGB-RTCORE-PURE-CANDIDATES-ZERO`) under the precise standalone-`#else` framing and **converged**: 37 `#ifdef HEXA_HAS_HEXA_RT_STDLIB` guarded blocks (35 with an `#else` arm, 2 native-only), 43 delegate-externs, ~40 guarded fns. **Decisive verification:** all 43 native-arm `rt_*` externs (`rt_null_coal`/`rt_len`/`rt_map_*`/`rt_print*`/`rt_cmp_*`/`rt_eq_*`/`rt_add_slow`/`rt_sub`/`rt_mul`/`rt_div`/`rt_mod`/…) already have a hexa-source body (`self/rt/core.hexa` · `stdlib/runtime/numeric.hexa`) = ALREADY-NATIVE. The auto-classifier flagged 6 `PURE?` candidates; reading each body settled them — `hexa_map_set`/`hexa_map_remove`→`_impl` raw-hashtable (ALLOC-WALLED), `hexa_println`→`printf`/`fflush`/`getenv` (stdio substrate), `hexa_to_string`→recursive buffer (ALLOC-WALLED), and the only two genuinely-pure ones (`hexa_null_coal`, `hexa_len`) delegate to `rt_null_coal`/`rt_len` which are ALREADY hexa-source (`self/rt/core.hexa:32,45`), so porting them = re-porting already-native work (the `index_of` trap r1 warned of). **PURE-PORTABLE (needs-a-port) bucket = 0.** The `#else` bodies (reached only when `HEXA_HAS_HEXA_RT_STDLIB` is undefined — the standalone smoke/release link, `runtime_core.c:3173`) are thus standalone-link duplicates of already-native code, not unportable bodies. **Conclusion:** the per-family native-seed-drop lever is EXHAUSTED (c16 TRUE-CEILING — no migratable body remains; what's left is already-native duplication or substrate). The only two remaining `ls`-reduction levers are both outside the per-family-drop scope: (i) `__hx_make_val` construct-unlock (array-r2 lane — releases the CONSTRUCT-WALLED arith/cmp/eq/to_string ~13 families) and (ii) standalone-`#else` dedup / `runtime.c` substrate redesign (the M5 standalone-redesign lane — a build redesign, not a port). No port was forced (c9); `runtime_core.c` byte delta = 0. m5 per-family-drop lane DEPLETED.

**Zero-C scope (Go/Rust-equivalent, clarified 2026-06-16):** "no `.c`" means the *user-visible* runtime (arena · tag · string/array · syscall · exception-dispatch) is native; the OS/ABI bootstrap floor — libm transcendentals and the Linux libc `setjmp`/`longjmp` — is the freestanding substrate every self-hosting runtime rests on (as do Go/Rust). **Exception model (RT-NATIVE Z4, closed):** `try`/`catch` lowers to a `setjmp`/`longjmp` try-stack; on **arm64-darwin** `hxlcl_setjmp`/`hxlcl_longjmp` are already **naked asm** (zero C, runtime.c cycle 86) — extractable to a `.s` file, so it does NOT block `ls self/*.c == ∅` on the primary target; on **x86_64-linux** it is a libc wrapper, kept as a platform floor (honest-keep, like libm). verdict `.verdicts/zeroc-breakthrough/F-RT-NATIVE-Z4-SETJMP-DECISION.txt`.

The atlas is consulted only at the S8 citation gate; once the gate passes, lowering and codegen run with no atlas dependency, so the produced binary carries zero verification overhead.
`hexa verify` is the single canonical verification surface and the project's g5 gate:

items: **S6 equational `@verify`** (in-compiler): canonicalizes LHS/RHS (const-fold, associativity, commutativity), checks equality, then does a deterministic sample-eval counter-example search. Failures surface as `HX6001` (normalization mismatch) or `HX6002` (witness found).
**S8 citation** (in-compiler): every formula-bearing function must resolve its cited `L[id]` in `static_atlas()`, with kind match and tombstone check, else fatal `HX8004`/`HX1099`.

**`hexa atlas verify` / `reverify`** (tool-level): recomputes atlas F/P nodes and reports `MATCH`/`DRIFT`/`UNVERIFIABLE` against the recorded claim (ε tolerance); a successful verify **auto-folds** the verified atom into the atlas (`embedded.gen.hexa`) — verify is ambient, not a separate `atlas register` ceremony.
